passages.text: In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, David sent out Joab and his servants with the whole army of Israel. They destroyed the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah, but David remained in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Spring was the time when kings usually went out to war.
David did not go to war himself.
David sent Joab to lead the army.
Joab was David’s commander.
David also sent his servants with Joab.
David sent the whole army of Israel with them.
The army fought against the Ammonites.
The army destroyed the Ammonites.
The army surrounded the city of Rabbah.
David stayed in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ לִתְשׁוּבַ֨ת הַשָּׁנָ֜ה לְעֵ֣ת׀ צֵ֣את הַמַּלְאֿכִ֗ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח דָּוִ֡ד אֶת־ יוֹאָב֩ וְאֶת־ עֲבָדָ֨יו עִמּ֜וֹ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיַּשְׁחִ֙תוּ֙ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיָּצֻ֖רוּ עַל־ רַבָּ֑ה וְדָוִ֖ד יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: One evening David got up from his bed and strolled around on the roof of the palace. And from the roof he saw a woman bathing—a very beautiful woman.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
One evening, David got up from his bed.
David walked on the roof of the palace.
From the roof, David saw a woman.
The woman was bathing.
The woman was very beautiful.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ לְעֵ֣ת הָעֶ֗רֶב וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד מֵעַ֤ל מִשְׁכָּבוֹ֙ וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ֙ עַל־ גַּ֣ג בֵּית־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּ֥רְא אִשָּׁ֛ה רֹחֶ֖צֶת מֵעַ֣ל הַגָּ֑ג וְהָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: So David sent and inquired about the woman, and he was told, “This is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David saw a woman bathing.
David wanted to know who she was.
David sent someone to ask about the woman.
The person told David about her.
The person said, “She is Bathsheba.”
“She is the daughter of Eliam.”
“She is the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּדְרֹ֖שׁ לָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲלוֹא־ זֹאת֙ בַּת־ שֶׁ֣בַע בַּת־ אֱלִיעָ֔ם אֵ֖שֶׁת אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Then David sent messengers to get her, and when she came to him, he slept with her. (Now she had just purified herself from her uncleanness.) Then she returned home.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David saw a woman named Bathsheba.
Bathsheba was very beautiful.
David sent messengers to bring Bathsheba to him.
Bathsheba came to David.
David slept with Bathsheba.
Bathsheba had just purified herself from her uncleanness.
Bathsheba returned to her home.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד מַלְאָכִ֜ים וַיִּקָּחֶ֗הָ וַתָּב֤וֹא אֵלָיו֙ וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמָּ֔הּ וְהִ֥יא מִתְקַדֶּ֖שֶׁת מִטֻּמְאָתָ֑הּ וַתָּ֖שָׁב אֶל־ בֵּיתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And the woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, “I am pregnant.”
passages.sermon:
Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
Bathsheba conceived a child.
Bathsheba sent a message to David.
Bathsheba said, “I am pregnant.”
passages.original: וַתַּ֖הַר הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתִּשְׁלַח֙ וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֔ד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הָרָ֥ה אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: At this, David sent orders to Joab: “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” So Joab sent him to David.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Uriah was a Hittite and a soldier in David’s army.
David sent a message to Joab.
David said, “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.”
Joab received David’s message.
Joab sent Uriah to David.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב שְׁלַ֣ח אֵלַ֔י אֶת־ אֽוּרִיָּ֖ה הַחִתִּ֑י וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־ אֽוּרִיָּ֖ה אֶל־ דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: When Uriah came to him, David asked how Joab and the troops were doing with the war.
passages.sermon:
Uriah came to David.
David spoke to Uriah.
David asked about Joab.
David asked about the people.
David asked about the war.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א אוּרִיָּ֖ה אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁאַ֣ל דָּוִ֗ד לִשְׁל֤וֹם יוֹאָב֙ וְלִשְׁל֣וֹם הָעָ֔ם וְלִשְׁל֖וֹם הַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Then he said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” So Uriah left the palace, and a gift from the king followed him.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Uriah the Hittite.
David said, “Go down to your house.”
David said, “Wash your feet.”
Uriah left the king’s house.
A gift from the king followed Uriah.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ לְא֣וּרִיָּ֔ה רֵ֥ד לְבֵיתְךָ֖ וּרְחַ֣ץ רַגְלֶ֑יךָ וַיֵּצֵ֤א אֽוּרִיָּה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתֵּצֵ֥א אַחֲרָ֖יו מַשְׂאַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: But Uriah slept at the door of the palace with all his master’s servants; he did not go down to his house.
passages.sermon:
Uriah was a soldier under King David.
Uriah did not go to his own house.
Uriah slept at the entrance of the king’s palace.
Uriah stayed there with all the other servants of his master.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב אוּרִיָּ֗ה פֶּ֚תַח בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־ עַבְדֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָרַ֖ד אֶל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And David was told, “Uriah did not go home.” “Haven’t you just arrived from a journey?” David asked Uriah. “Why didn’t you go home?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Uriah was one of David’s soldiers.
Someone told David, “Uriah did not go to his house.”
David spoke to Uriah.
David said, “You have just come from a journey.”
David asked, “Why did you not go to your house?”
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְדָוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־ יָרַ֥ד אוּרִיָּ֖ה אֶל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ אוּרִיָּ֗ה הֲל֤וֹא מִדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ אַתָּ֣ה בָ֔א מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹֽא־ יָרַ֥דְתָּ אֶל־ בֵּיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Uriah answered, “The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in tents, and my master Joab and his soldiers are camped in the open field. How can I go to my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? As surely as you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing!”
passages.sermon:
Uriah was a soldier under King David.
Uriah spoke to David.
Uriah said, “The Ark is staying in a tent.
Israel is staying in tents.
Judah is staying in tents.
My master Joab is in the field.
The servants of my master are camped in the open field.
I am a soldier like them.
Should I go to my house?
Should I eat and drink at home?
Should I sleep with my wife while they are in the field?
As surely as you live, I will not do this thing.
As surely as your soul lives, I will not do this thing.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אוּרִיָּ֜ה אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד הָ֠אָרוֹן וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל וִֽיהוּדָ֜ה יֹשְׁבִ֣ים בַּסֻּכּ֗וֹת וַאדֹנִ֨י יוֹאָ֜ב וְעַבְדֵ֤י אֲדֹנִ֨י עַל־ פְּנֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ חֹנִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֞י אָב֧וֹא אֶל־ בֵּיתִ֛י לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת וְלִשְׁכַּ֣ב עִם־ אִשְׁתִּ֑י חַיֶּ֙ךָ֙ וְחֵ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ אִֽם־ אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: “Stay here one more day,” David said to Uriah, “and tomorrow I will send you back.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to Uriah.
David said, “Stay here today also.
Tomorrow I will send you back.”
Uriah obeyed David.
Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day.
Uriah also stayed in Jerusalem the next day.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ אוּרִיָּ֗ה שֵׁ֥ב בָּזֶ֛ה גַּם־ הַיּ֖וֹם וּמָחָ֣ר אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֑ךָּ וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב אוּרִיָּ֧ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וּמִֽמָּחֳרָֽת׃

passages.text: Then David invited Uriah to eat and drink with him, and he got Uriah drunk. And in the evening Uriah went out to lie down on his cot with his master’s servants, but he did not go home.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David called Uriah to him.
David invited Uriah to eat in his presence.
David gave Uriah food and drink.
David made Uriah drunk.
In the evening, Uriah left David’s house.
Uriah lay down to sleep on his bed.
Uriah slept with the servants of his master.
Uriah did not go down to his own house.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָא־ ל֣וֹ דָוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֧אכַל לְפָנָ֛יו וַיֵּ֖שְׁתְּ וַֽיְשַׁכְּרֵ֑הוּ וַיֵּצֵ֣א בָעֶ֗רֶב לִשְׁכַּ֤ב בְּמִשְׁכָּבוֹ֙ עִם־ עַבְדֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֔יו וְאֶל־ בֵּית֖וֹ לֹ֥א יָרָֽד׃

passages.text: The next morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Uriah was a soldier in David’s army.
In the morning, David wrote a letter.
David addressed the letter to Joab.
David gave the letter to Uriah.
David sent Uriah to deliver the letter to Joab.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּכְתֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֛ד סֵ֖פֶר אֶל־ יוֹאָ֑ב וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח בְּיַ֥ד אוּרִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: In the letter he wrote: “Put Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle; then withdraw from him, so that he may be struck down and killed.”
passages.sermon:
King David wrote a letter to Joab.
David gave instructions about Uriah the Hittite.
David said, “Place Uriah at the front lines of the fiercest battle.
Then pull back from him.
Let Uriah be attacked.
Let Uriah be killed.”
passages.original: וַיִּכְתֹּ֥ב בַּסֵּ֖פֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר הָב֣וּ אֶת־ אֽוּרִיָּ֗ה אֶל־ מוּל֙ פְּנֵ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הַֽחֲזָקָ֔ה וְשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם מֵאַחֲרָ֖יו וְנִכָּ֥ה וָמֵֽת׃ס

passages.text: So as Joab besieged the city, he assigned Uriah to a place where he saw the strongest enemy soldiers.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab watched the city closely.
Joab led the siege against the city.
Joab chose a place near the city walls.
Joab knew strong enemy soldiers were there.
Joab put Uriah in that place.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י בִּשְׁמ֥וֹר יוֹאָ֖ב אֶל־ הָעִ֑יר וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־ א֣וּרִיָּ֔ה אֶל־ הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י אַנְשֵׁי־ חַ֖יִל שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: And when the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of David’s servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite also died.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
The men of the city came out from their city.
They fought against Joab and his soldiers.
Some of David’s servants died in the battle.
Uriah the Hittite also died in the battle.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨צְא֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ וַיִּלָּחֲמ֣וּ אֶת־ יוֹאָ֔ב וַיִּפֹּ֥ל מִן־ הָעָ֖ם מֵעַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיָּ֕מָת גַּ֖ם אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Joab sent to David a full account of the battle and instructed the messenger, “When you have finished giving the king all the details of the battle, if the king’s anger flares, he may ask you, ‘Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Did you not realize they would shoot from atop the wall?
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab sent a message to King David.
Joab told David everything about the battle.
Joab gave instructions to the messenger.
Joab said, “When you finish telling the king all the details of the battle, listen to his response.”
Joab warned the messenger about the king’s possible anger.
Joab said, “If the king becomes angry, he may ask you a question.”
Joab said, “The king may ask, ‘Why did you go so close to the city to fight?’”
Joab said, “The king may also ask, ‘Did you not know they would shoot arrows from the top of the wall?’”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח יוֹאָ֑ב וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֔ד אֶת־ כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֖י הַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃ וַיְצַ֥ו אֶת־ הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּכַלּוֹתְךָ֗ אֵ֛ת כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וְהָיָ֗ה אִֽם־ תַּעֲלֶה֙ חֲמַ֣ת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאָמַ֣ר לְךָ֔ מַדּ֛וּעַ נִגַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֶל־ הָעִ֖יר לְהִלָּחֵ֑ם הֲל֣וֹא יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ יֹר֖וּ מֵעַ֥ל הַחוֹמָֽה׃

passages.text: Who was the one to strike Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth ? Was it not a woman who dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you get so close to the wall?’ If so, then you are to say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the son of Jerubbesheth.
Someone struck Abimelech.
A woman threw an upper millstone on Abimelech from the wall.
The millstone hit Abimelech.
Abimelech died in Thebez.
You went close to the wall.
Why did you go so close to the wall?
You must say this:
Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
passages.original: מִֽי־ הִכָּ֞ה אֶת־ אֲבִימֶ֣לֶךְ בֶּן־ יְרֻבֶּ֗שֶׁת הֲלֽוֹא־ אִשָּׁ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יכָה עָלָיו֩ פֶּ֨לַח רֶ֜כֶב מֵעַ֤ל הַֽחוֹמָה֙ וַיָּ֣מָת בְּתֵבֵ֔ץ לָ֥מָּה נִגַּשְׁתֶּ֖ם אֶל־ הַֽחוֹמָ֑ה וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ גַּ֗ם עַבְדְּךָ֛ אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּ֖י מֵֽת׃

passages.text: So the messenger set out and reported to David all that Joab had sent him to say.
passages.sermon: A messenger left Joab.\r\nThe messenger went to David.\r\nThe messenger told David everything Joab had instructed him to say.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הַמַּלְאָ֑ךְ וַיָּבֹא֙ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֔ד אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁלָח֖וֹ יוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: The messenger said to David, “The men overpowered us and came out against us in the field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.
passages.sermon:
The messenger spoke to David.
He said, “The men overpowered us.
They came out against us in the field.
We fought them there.
We pushed them back.
We drove them to the entrance of the gate.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמַּלְאָךְ֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד כִּֽי־ גָבְר֤וּ עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיֵּצְא֥וּ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַנִּהְיֶ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עַד־ פֶּ֥תַח הַשָּֽׁעַר׃

passages.text: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king’s servants were killed. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.”
passages.sermon:
The archers stood on top of the wall.
The archers shot arrows at your servants.
Some of the king’s servants died.
Your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.
passages.original: וַיֹּרְאוּ הַמּוֹרְאִים אֶל־ עֲבָדֶ֙ךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַחוֹמָ֔ה וַיָּמ֖וּתוּ מֵעַבְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְגַ֗ם עַבְדְּךָ֛ אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּ֖י מֵֽת׃ס

passages.text: Then David told the messenger, “Say this to Joab: ‘Do not let this matter upset you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Strengthen your attack against the city and demolish it.’ Encourage him with these words.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to the messenger.
David gave the messenger instructions for Joab.
David said, “Tell Joab this.
Do not let this matter trouble you.
The sword kills one person as well as another.
Make your attack against the city stronger.
Destroy the city.
Encourage Joab with these words.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ הַמַּלְאָ֗ךְ כֹּֽה־ תֹאמַ֤ר אֶל־ יוֹאָב֙ אַל־ יֵרַ֤ע בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־ כָזֹ֥ה וְכָזֶ֖ה תֹּאכַ֣ל הֶחָ֑רֶב הַחֲזֵ֨ק מִלְחַמְתְּךָ֧ אֶל־ הָעִ֛יר וְהָרְסָ֖הּ וְחַזְּקֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
passages.sermon:
Uriah was a Hittite man.
Uriah served as a soldier for King David.
Uriah had a wife.
Uriah died in battle.
Uriah’s wife heard that her husband Uriah was dead.
Uriah’s wife mourned for her husband.
passages.original: וַתִּשְׁמַע֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת אֽוּרִיָּ֔ה כִּי־ מֵ֖ת אוּרִיָּ֣ה אִישָׁ֑הּ וַתִּסְפֹּ֖ד עַל־ בַּעְלָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And when the time of mourning was over, David had her brought to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Uriah’s wife finished mourning for her husband.
David sent for her.
David brought her into his house.
She became David’s wife.
She gave birth to a son for David.
The LORD saw what David had done.
The LORD considered David’s action evil.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר הָאֵ֗בֶל וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח דָּוִ֜ד וַיַּאַסְפָ֤הּ אֶל־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ וַתְּהִי־ ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד ל֖וֹ בֵּ֑ן וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה דָוִ֖ד בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
